production.note: US model years 2020 to 2023. First: pcna-2020-718-cayman-gt4 introduces "The 2020 Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 and 718 Spyder", "expected to reach U.S. dealers in spring 2020". Last: kbb-2023-718-cayman lists a 2023 "Cayman GT4" with 414 horsepower, and Kelley Blue Book's 2024 page says "The GT4 and T versions have been discontinued." The separate GT4 RS continued.

body.note: Kelley Blue Book lists 718 Cayman trims as "Coupe 2D". The open car is sold under its own name (718 Spyder).

configuration.note: Spec sheet: "Six-cylinder naturally aspirated boxer engine"

aspiration.note: Spec sheet: "Six-cylinder naturally aspirated boxer engine"

fuel.note: Inferred from the spec sheet's description of a naturally aspirated boxer engine with a 16.9 gal fuel tank; no hybrid system is described.

transmission.note: Launched for 2020 with the manual only (spec sheet porsche-2020-718-gt4-us-specs: "6-speed manual transmission with dual-mass flywheel"). PDK was added for model year 2021; PCNA: the 4.0-liter 718 models "have been available to order with the optional seven-speed Porsche dual-clutch transmission (PDK) since June" and the GT models are quicker "than with the standard six-speed manual transmission." DCT is Porsche PDK.

powerHp.note: Quote: "Max. power output at engine speed 414 hp 7,600 rpm". Corroborated by pcna-2020-718-cayman-gt4: "developing 414 horsepower and 309 lb.-ft. of torque". Unchanged for 2021 (pcna-2021-718-pdk: "the 414 hp GT models").

weightLb.note: Coupe with the 6-speed manual, the only transmission in model year 2020. Quote: "Curb weight 3,199 lbs. 3,206 lbs." under the columns "718 Cayman GT4 | 718 Spyder". No Porsche figure for the PDK car was opened.
